first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4-6% QoQ, suggesting friction in early user experience. Memory_31 and memory_86 both show that simplification drives measurable gains in activation and completion, with durable effects and no documented retention harm. This directly addresses the current metric declines. I'm verifying these two to confirm the magnitude and ensure conditions (SMB focus, field reduction approach) are transferable to current cohorts. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because memory_73 explicitly flags retention harm and warns against generalization as growth strategy—the risk to long-term qualified revenue is too high. Referral incentive (memory_57) is lower-leverage for acute activation decline. Activation messaging (memory_91) is secondary—fixing the funnel friction first is more foundational. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is misaligned with the SMB-skewed activation problem. Standard experiment scale balances learning velocity against the week's constraint.

final.rationale: Archive confirms both memories. Memory_31 shows signup simplification drove +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue with only -1% retention risk on SMB. Memory_86 shows onboarding shortening lifted completion +13% and time-to-value by 2.1 days, with +3% retention gain. Current situation shows activation down 6% and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Simplifying onboarding directly addresses both metrics and carries the strongest evidence base: low retention downside (actually positive in memory_86), proven effectiveness, and no documented harm to long-term value. This is lower-risk than promotional pricing (memory_73 flagged retention damage) and more directly applicable than referral or messaging approaches. Standard experiment scale allows learning this week while preserving option value if results warrant broader rollout.
